durotar_tiragarde_approach.description:
Watchwarden Kelgrim. Keep low coming up - they've got rifles on that wall and too much time.

I've held this post longer than I'm willing to put a number to.

The humans washed up here years back. Kul Tiras sailors - shipwrecked, marooned, nobody's ever got a straight answer out of a survivor before putting him down, and I include myself in that.

They dug in. Built walls out of the keep's old stones, which I'll admit was good work.

Now they raid the coast road when they're hungry, and they are hungry often.

I don't call them monsters. I'm careful about that word and I'd ask you to be too.

I call them the stranded.

Thin the outer wall. Marines, deckhands, whoever's standing the watch.

And leave the one who commands them. Not out of mercy - because that conversation deserves better than me shouting it at you between sword-swings.
durotar_tiragarde_approach.accept_text: The outer wall. Whichever kind you find first. Don't go near the one who commands them - not yet.
durotar_tiragarde_approach.turn_in_text:
Good. You didn't hesitate, which tells me something about you, though I couldn't say what yet.

Sit a moment before you go back in.

There's still the matter of their captain.

durotar_tiragarde_captain.description:
[Kelgrim takes his time.]

Captain Thalenvorde commands what's left of that garrison, and I've been putting this conversation off since you first walked up here.

Here's the whole of it.

Thalenvorde is a person.

Not a boar. Not a demon pulled out of a tear in the world that was never going to have a name until somebody asked. A person, with a rank and a crew and - however he ended up on this coast - a life before it that I'd guess looked fairly ordinary.

I've killed enough of the stranded that it stopped having weight for me years ago. I'm not proud of the arithmetic and I'm not ashamed of it either.

But killing a beast doesn't ask anything of you. Killing a person does.

I'm not going to talk you out of it. The garrison won't stop raiding while he commands it, and out here that's reason enough.

I just wanted you walking in knowing what you're about to do, rather than finding out afterward.

That's the only kindness I've got today.
durotar_tiragarde_captain.accept_text: Inside the keep, at the heart of the garrison. He bleeds the way you do.
durotar_tiragarde_captain.turn_in_text:
It's done, then.

I can see it on you. That particular quiet that comes after - I remember mine, if you can believe an orc admitting to it.

He won't be leading raids on the coast road. The valley's safer for it. That part is true and it matters.

Keep what you took off him. Not as a trophy. As a reminder of where you stand now, if you find you need one.

You crossed a line today that doesn't uncross. Most of us out here crossed it a long time before you got here.

Now you know what it actually weighs. That's not nothing, and I won't pretend it is.
